annotation.title_clean: Robots, Autonomous Systems, AI, and the Debate About a Limited Form of Legal Personality
annotation.title_en: Robots, Autonomous Systems, AI, and the Debate About a Limited Form of Legal Personality
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366: Social Robots in Social Institutions (Robophilosophy 2022), IOS Press
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2022 paper arguing that the closed reaction to the European Parliament's 2017 call to explore electronic personhood for sophisticated autonomous robots should be critically re-examined, considering civil and criminal liability. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: There may be good reasons to deny legal personality to autonomous systems, but none for avoiding the debate.
The European Parliament in Feb 2017 asked the Commission to explore a specific legal status for robots as electronic persons liable for damage.
The reaction to this proposal was complete closure.
The grounds for opposition should be re-examined in light of civil and criminal liability.
